name: Aros the Spiritmaster

facts.text: Aros the Spiritmaster is the level-72 final of Dodens Gruva with 40,000 health.
He raises a spirit champion that fights beside him and stuns; both are linked, so pulling one brings the other.
He performs rituals, debuffs spirit resistance (Negate Spirit), casts Extinguish Lifeforce and detonates Soul Annihilation (1,400 damage in an 800 radius).
He cries 'You will remember my name!' as he fights.
Allakhazam lists him at level 72 in Dodens Gruva; a later visitor remembered him as 'insta death' and sprinting through his room.
A guild beat Aros with three full groups in January 2003, after an earlier three-group defeat.
The Havamal says cattle die and kin die, but a good name never dies.
Aros is also an old Swedish and Danish place name, meaning a river mouth (to verify).

story:
Jarl Ormarr dug for iron under the Jamtland hills because a jarl needs iron to stay a jarl. His spiritmaster Aros stood at the shaft each morning and read the names of the shift aloud, and promised every man who went down that if he died in the dark he would be remembered. The skalds say a good name is the one thing that does not die. Aros believed it.

Then the mine broke into a cold seam, and the cold seam opened on a hall below where something was calling the dead. The miners died, and their dead rose and began to walk downward, toward the calling. Aros kept his promise the only way he could. He bound them: to the mine, to their picks, to him, so that they would never be forgotten because they would never be gone, and so that whatever called from below could not have them. He bound himself with them. Somewhere in the binding he forgot the word good.

He fights as he lived, by ritual. His spirit champion rises at his side, the strongest of the shift, and stands between him and you. He strips away your guard against the spirit world, and then he spends himself in a burst that empties a room. And he tells every one of you the same thing. You will remember his name. You usually do.
legend: Three groups beat him, but only the second time. His spirit champion comes with him: hold it, stun-break, and kill Aros through it. Spread out before his Soul Annihilation, which hits the whole room, and keep spirit resists up against his debuff. Say a dead friend's name aloud down there and Aros will learn it.

loremasterTopic.text: Jarl Ormarr's spiritmaster, who read the names of the shift at the shaft and promised each man he would be remembered. When the dead began walking down toward a [calling] below, he bound them to the mine, and himself with them. The skalds say a good name never dies. Aros kept the names and forgot the word good.

bookPage: Here are the names of the shift that went down to the cold seam: Hamar, Bjorn the Younger, Kol, Ulf Half-hand, and the jarl's hound Gudlaugr, who would not be left behind. The spiritmaster read them out at the shaft and said none would be forgotten. That was the last tally. Whoever finds this slate: we are not forgotten. We are still digging. Something below is calling us, and Aros will not let us answer. We do not know which of them to thank. Do not read our names aloud.
